summary.headline: Allcargo Q2 FY27 revenue rose 3.4% YoY to INR555 crore while EBITDA grew 24.2% to INR77 crore, margin 13.9%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a two-phase quarter: soft demand in July and August, then a visible September pickup that management says continued into October. Revenue from operations was INR555 crore (up 3.4% YoY, up 1.6% QoQ), with gross margin at 31.4% and EBITDA margin at 13.9%. Management attributed margin expansion mainly to service-led price realisation and tight cost control, and reiterated its FY28 revenue guidance. Express volumes were described as stabilised after a decline, with higher realisation per ton.

segments.name: Express Logistics
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 7.7% YoY and volumes have stabilised after earlier declines; realisation per ton indexed at about 107.5. H1 EBITDA margin 6.5% and gross margin 27%.

segments.name: Consultative Logistics (CL)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 5.8% YoY in Q2. H1 gross margin 36.5% and EBITDA margin 29.7% (Ind AS), or 8.8% pre-Ind AS. Management cites e-commerce, auto engineering and chemicals as strongest verticals.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of 10% 3-year CAGR and 12% 5-year CAGR (from the prior analyst meet) reiterated; H1 revenue growth is about 7%-plus, and management expects a strong festive Q3 and year-end.
EBITDA margin aspiration of 15% (Ind AS) by FY28, from 13.5% in H1 FY27; management says the FY28 13%-plus target is already met on the current base.
Gross margin guidance: 10% CAGR over 3 years, rising to 15% over 5 years; PBT CAGR of 20% over 5 years.
Pre-Ind AS operating EBITDA for FY28 can be assumed at about 5%, per management.
Growth ambition is to outgrow the market by 1 percentage point in both Express and CL.
Capex: Express about INR15-20 crore per year including hub and expansion capex; CL capex about INR20 crore one year out, largely via operating lease model.
Vijay Nehra to become MD and CEO from 1 January 2027; Ketan Kulkarni moves to an Allcargo Group role.
capex_capacity: Express capex about INR15 crore per year historically; FY27 expected INR15-20 crore, covering hub-related and expansion capex.
CL capex is tied to new business wins and new warehouses, funded via operating lease pipeline; about INR20 crore expected one year out.
Management says the company is pruning suboptimal warehouse and contract portfolio and avoiding holding empty square footage.
Warehousing space under management was down 5.5% YoY, per an analyst question; management did not dispute this figure.
New AI-enabled booking application rolled out this quarter to cut manual intervention and cost to serve.
demand_pricing: July-August demand was soft across several corridors; September showed a visible pickup, and October was described as very strong.
Management is prioritising service-led pricing and says it will not compromise yield for volume; price correction was implemented over Q1 and Q2.
Net service level index about 110.2 in Q2 FY27 (management's measure of operating quality).
Express new business in October was the highest ever added in company history, per management.
E-way bill generation crossed 141 million run rate; GST collections up 14.7% YoY in September (management-cited macro indicators). India Q1 GDP growth stated at 7.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Express and CL volumes declining when peers are growing, and what are the expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is deliberately upgrading portfolio mix; Express revenue grew 7.7% YoY, volumes have stabilised, and realisation per ton rose to about 107.5 index. It declined to chase low-margin tonnage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Consultative Logistics margins on an EBITDA basis, and what is the pre-Ind AS figure?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 CL EBITDA margin is 29.7% on Ind AS and 8.8% pre-Ind AS; Express is 6.5% on Ind AS. Gross margin for H1 is 36.5% for CL and 27% for Express.

qa_highlights.question: Which customer segments and service lines are seeing the strongest demand?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is strongest, followed by auto engineering and chemicals; warehousing and transportation are the strongest solution lines. These three verticals will be the focus for the next 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 3-5 year growth, margin and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue CAGR of 10% over 3 years and 12% over 5 years; gross margin CAGR 10% over 3 years rising to 15% over 5; PBT CAGR 20% over 5 years. Annual capex is about INR15-20 crore for Express and about INR20 crore for CL.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the EBITDA margin and what is the operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price correction drove most of the 24% YoY EBITDA growth; QoQ EBITDA rose 8.5%, with gross profit up 6.5%. H1 EBITDA grew about 30% against revenue and gross margin growth of about 12%, implying 18% from operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY28 guidance still hold, and can revenue growth exceed the 10%-12% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the revenue guidance, citing H1 growth of about 7%-plus and expected festive-quarter strength. It said the FY28 13%-plus EBITDA margin is already met, with 15% now the aspiration.

risks_watch: H1 revenue growth of about 7% is below the 10%-12% CAGR guidance; reaching the target requires a sharp acceleration in H2.
Express volume decline and warehousing space under management down 5.5% YoY, despite pruning and portfolio-upgrade commentary.
Pre-Ind AS CL EBITDA margin of 8.8% versus 29.7% on Ind AS shows heavy lease-accounting impact; the gap matters for valuation.
Leadership transition: Vijay Nehra becomes MD and CEO on 1 January 2027.
Competitive intensity in contract logistics and pricing pressure; management says it will continue pruning suboptimal contracts.
Monitor Q3 festive-season volume and whether October momentum holds.
Separate Allcargo Global call scheduled; the group's other entity's results may affect the consolidated picture.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and pricing discipline, with clear reiteration of the FY28 framework. Cautious on volumes: management acknowledged soft July-August demand and Express volume weakness, and avoided committing to a volume-growth number beyond saying October was strong.
key_quotes: We will not compromise on yields for indiscriminate growth.
chasing unviable low-margin tonnage destroys long-term value.
So the guidance from the investor presentation remains as of today on the revenue that we had given. We are confident of achieving that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Ind AS EBITDA margin 13.9% in Q2 (+240 bps YoY, +90 bps QoQ) and H1 at 13.5%, driven by service-led price correction and cost control; management targets 15% by FY28 and says the 13%-plus target is already met.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Express capex of INR15-20 crore per year and CL warehouses tied to new wins (~INR20 crore one year out), but no capacity count given and warehouse space under management fell 5.5% YoY.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Express volumes only stabilised after declines and H1 revenue growth is about 7%, with October described as very strong and a record month for Express new business, but management avoided a volume-growth number.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure disclosed, so the capex call rests on the CL warehouse pipeline (~INR20 crore expected one year out) and the stated Express run-rate of INR15-20 crore per year, not on a capacity squeeze.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue guidance of 10% 3-year and 12% 5-year CAGR was only reiterated, and H1 growth of about 7% would need a sharp H2 acceleration to reach it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue growth of about 7% sits below the 10%-12% CAGR guidance, and warehouse space under management is down 5.5% YoY, so the revenue target carries execution risk.

rows.label: AI-enabled booking application cutting manual intervention
rows.why: Rolled out this quarter to cut manual intervention and cost to serve; no savings amount was given.

rows.label: Service-led price realisation in Express and CL
rows.why: Price correction implemented over Q1 and Q2, with Express realisation per ton indexed at about 107.5 and management refusing to trade yield for volume.

rows.label: Pruning of suboptimal warehouse and contract portfolio
rows.why: Management is exiting low-margin contracts and avoiding empty square footage, which supports margins but is the reason warehouse space fell 5.5% YoY.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin expansion from pricing discipline and reiterated the FY28 framework, but cautious on volumes after soft July-August demand and Express volume weakness.
